name: Charles Kains-Jackson
bio: London solicitor specialising in literary matters (1857-1933), and from 1888 to 1894 editor of The Artist and Journal of Home Culture - a magazine which, in the editors' own words, he used in part as a forum for London's homosexual coterie, and to which Lord Alfred Douglas contributed. Wilde consulted him professionally over Salomé in November 1893.
bio_note: The volume's Index of Recipients. The description of His magazine is the editors' own and is quoted rather than paraphrased - 'which he used in part as a forum for London's homosexual coterie' (printed 574, note 1). Two items at printed 574 and 576. His own circle - the Uranian poets, and his editorship's place in that literature - lies outside this volume and is not asserted here.
